housing: Westmorland and Furness was formed in 2023 from Barrow-in-Furness, Eden and South Lakeland. Barrow has dense Victorian terraces built for the shipyards, a large private rented sector and growing numbers of HMOs. South Lakeland and Eden are dominated by stone cottages, farmhouses and Victorian villas, and in the Lake District many homes are second homes or holiday lets, which keeps long-term lets scarce. Many rural homes are off the gas network.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Barrow: photograph damp in back kitchens, rear yards, back alleys and older sash or replacement windows.
Stone cottages in the Lakes and Eden valley: record damp, condensation and mould, which are common in solid-walled homes in a wet climate.
Rural homes off the gas network: note the oil tank level, solid-fuel stoves, private water supplies and septic tanks.
Coastal homes on Walney and around Morecambe Bay: photograph metalwork, window frames and render for salt and storm damage.
Homes in flood-hit towns such as Kendal and Appleby: check for flood damage, airbricks, flood doors and watermarks.
Former holiday lets now let long-term: record every item of furniture and equipment, as inventories can be long.
tenantHelp: Westmorland and Furness Council's private sector housing team deals with disrepair and unsafe conditions in private rented homes and licenses HMOs.
